items.prompt: Water moves through a plant. Put the places in order, starting in the soil.
hints: Water starts outside the plant.
Follow the water from the bottom of the plant to the top.
After the soil, which part does the water go into first?
items.explanation: Water goes from the soil into the roots. It travels up the stem and reaches the leaves.

items.prompt: Which part of a plant carries water up from the roots to the leaves?

options.why: The flower makes seeds. It gets water from the stem too.
A seed is not part of a grown plant's water path.
Soil holds water, but it is not part of the plant.

hints: Think about the part between the roots and the leaves.
This part works like a pipe.
Trace a line from the roots up to a leaf. What do you pass through?
items.explanation: The stem has tiny tubes inside. They carry water from the roots up to the leaves and flowers.

items.prompt: Water enters a plant through its ___.
hints: Water is in the soil.
Which part of the plant is in the soil?
This part grows downwards from the bottom of the stem.
items.explanation: Roots grow in the soil and take in water. The water then travels up the stem.

items.prompt: Ana stands a white flower in a glass of blue water. What will she see the next day?

figure.alt: A white flower with its stem standing in a glass of blue water.

options.text: petals that are still pure white
options.why: The blue water travels up the stem, so colour reaches the petals.

options.text: blue colour only at the bottom of the stem
options.why: The water travels all the way up the stem to the petals.

options.text: new roots growing from the stem
options.why: One day is far too short for new roots to grow.

hints: The flower takes in the water it stands in.
Think about where the water travels once it is inside the stem.
Follow the blue water from the glass up the stem.
items.explanation: The flower takes up the blue water through its stem. The water travels to the petals, so they turn blue.

items.prompt: Bima stands a celery stalk in red water. Later he cuts it across and sees red dots. What are they?

options.text: tiny tubes that carried the red water up

options.why: Seeds are made in flowers, not inside celery stalks.
The red colour shows where water travelled, not insect holes.
Leaves make the food. The red shows where water moved.

hints: The red colour came from the water.
Think about how water travels up a stalk.
Ask yourself: what would carry water, like a straw?
items.explanation: The red dots are the ends of tiny tubes. These tubes carry water up the stalk, so they turned red.

items.prompt: A potted plant has had no water for a week. What do its leaves look like?

options.why: Without water, a plant cannot stay firm or grow well.
A plant with no water is struggling. It does not suddenly flower.
Plants need water to stay firm. Without it, they droop.

hints: Water helps a plant stay firm.
Think about a plant that has been forgotten on a hot day.
Picture the leaves when the water inside them runs out.
items.explanation: Water inside a plant keeps its stem and leaves firm. Without water, the plant wilts and its leaves droop.

items.prompt: A wilted plant is watered. A few hours later it stands up again. Why?

options.text: It grows a set of new leaves very quickly.
options.why: New leaves take days to grow. The old leaves fill with water again.

options.text: The soil pushes the plant back up.
options.why: Soil does not push plants. Water inside the plant makes it firm.

options.text: Water travels up the stem and makes the plant firm again.
Sunlight makes the stem stronger straight away.
options.why: Light helps a plant make food, but the quick change comes from water.

hints: Think about what the plant was missing.
Remember the path water takes inside a plant.
Ask: where does the new water go after it enters the roots?
items.explanation: The roots take in the water. It travels up the stem into the leaves, which become firm again.

items.prompt: Pak Darto waters his chilli plants. Where is the best place to pour the water?

options.why: Flowers do not take in water for the whole plant.
Leaves take in very little water. Most water enters through the roots.
The fruit does not take in water for the plant.

options.text: on the soil around the roots

hints: Think about which part takes in water.
Where is that part of the plant?
Water needs to reach the part hidden in the soil.
items.explanation: Most water enters a plant through its roots. Pouring water on the soil lets it soak down to the roots.

items.prompt: Choose 2 reasons why a plant needs water.

options.why: Water does not decide how flowers smell.
Water does not keep birds away from a plant.

options.text: to help its leaves make food

options.why: Water helps roots grow. It does not stop them.

hints: Think about what happens to a plant with no water.
Remember what leaves need to make food.
Look for one reason about shape and one about food.
items.explanation: Water keeps a plant firm so it can stand up. Leaves also use water, with light and air, to make food.

items.prompt: Hana ties a clear plastic bag over some leaves on a sunny day. Later, water drops form inside. Where did the water come from?

options.why: The bag was dry. Plastic does not make water.
The Sun gives light and warmth, not water.
The bag was closed, and it was a sunny day.

hints: The bag was dry and closed.
Remember where water ends up after it travels up the stem.
Think about what was inside the bag with the air.
items.explanation: Water travels up the stem to the leaves. Some of it escapes from the leaves into the air and collects as drops on the bag.

items.prompt: Two celery stalks stand in red water. Stalk A has leaves. Stalk B has no leaves. Which turns red higher up first?

options.text: Stalk B, because it has fewer parts to fill
options.why: Leaves help pull water up. Without them, water rises more slowly.

options.text: Stalk A, because water leaving the leaves pulls more water up
both at the same speed, because water just soaks up
options.why: Leaves lose water into the air, and this pulls more water up the stalk.

options.text: neither, because celery cannot carry water
options.why: Celery stalks have tiny tubes that carry water.

hints: Think about what the leaves do with water.
Water escapes from leaves into the air.
If water leaves from the top, what happens to the water below it?
items.explanation: Water escapes from leaves into the air. This pulls more water up the tubes, so the stalk with leaves turns red higher up first.

items.prompt: Explain how water gets from the soil to a leaf. Use the words roots and stem.

criteria.label: Says water enters through the roots
Says water travels up the stem

planning: How does it get up to the leaf?
items.model: First, the roots take in water from the soil. Then the water travels up tiny tubes inside the stem. Finally, the water reaches the leaves, where it helps make food.
hints: Start where the water is: the soil.
Use the words first, then and finally.
items.explanation: Water enters the roots from the soil. It travels up tiny tubes in the stem until it reaches the leaves.
